//: THE REFERENCE EXAMPLE. Read this file first. It re-creates the game's starter pickup (the Junker: a battered seventies pickup,
stubby and boxy, with a lumpy load under a tarpaulin) using only the kit's format. Every '//' field is a comment: the checker ignores it.
Axes: x across (+x is the car's LEFT), y up (the ground is y = 0), z along (the nose at +z). Metres. Angles in degrees.
How it is built: a few big solid shapes, each a closed volume, overlapping where they join (overlap is fine, touching faces in one
plane are not); the paint (role body) on the big shapes, a second livery colour (role accent) on the roof, bonnet crown and rails.
name: Junker
description: A battered seventies pickup: square cab, flat wide face with stacked round lamps, a real bed with a tarpaulin load.

colors.//: custom flat colours, used as role 'paint:<name>'. Good / Evil may differ (the tarpaulin does).

parts.//: THE BODY: one flat-sided slab, side view extruded across the car. The outline is the side view (z, y) in order round it; the bevel rounds every edge by 4 cm and GROWS the outline by 4 cm, so the flanks end at x = +-1.0 for width 2.0. Low at the front (y 0.92) where the bonnet and wings sit on it, up to 1.18 under the cab.
parts.name: body

parts.//: THE BED: a LOFT through two equal cross-sections (a U: walls and the floor between them). 'half' is the +x half of the section from the bottom middle round to the top middle (here the floor's middle); the -x half is mirrored. Its flanks stand 4 mm inside the body's (0.996, not 1.0) so the two flanks never lie in one plane where they overlap (z-fighting).
parts.name: bed

parts.//: rolled top rails over the bed walls, a centimetre proud of the flank, in the accent shade
parts.name: bed rail

parts.//: the rear wheel tubs inside the bed: a half disc in side view, extruded 28 cm across (a closed solid, not an open half drum)
parts.name: wheel tub

parts.//: the tailgate between the lamp posts, up to the rails
parts.name: tailgate

parts.//: THE WINGS: raised a little over the bonnet's edges and rounded down at the front (a corner radius as the third number of a point: [z, y, r])
parts.name: wing

parts.//: THE BONNET: crowned (higher down its middle): a loft of its cross-section along z, in the accent shade
parts.name: bonnet

parts.//: THE CAB: square, close behind the bonnet; its front face is raked at the same angle as the windscreen that lies on it
parts.name: cab

parts.//: a flat roof overhanging the cab, the accent shade; it is the ROOF mount's surface
parts.name: cab roof

parts.//: GLASS ON THE COWL: the windscreen is a thin slab (2 cm) tipped to the cab's own rake (atan(0.6 / 0.34) = 60.5 degrees; rot x > 0 drops the front edge) and laid 3 cm out from the cab's front face, so it sits ON the body with no gap and no shared plane. Its foot is on the cowl, its top under the roof's overhang.
parts.name: windscreen

parts.//: side glass: a 2 cm prism of the window's side view, standing 1.6 cm proud of the cab's flank (x 0.95). The window outline follows the cab's front pillar (the same rake) at an even distance.
parts.name: side window

parts.//: the cab's rear window, seen over the bed
parts.name: rear window

parts.//: THE FACE: a chrome-framed grille of upright bars, raked forward a little (rot x 5.7)
parts.name: grille frame

parts.//: lamp pods either side of the grille: a loft of rounded rectangles (the outer sections smaller: a bevelled edge)
parts.name: lamp pod

parts.//: two round lamps stacked in each pod: a chrome rim, the lens 1 cm proud of it (never flush: flush faces fight)
parts.name: lamp rim

parts.//: a steel bumper bar wrapping the corners (the ends turned 40 degrees about y; the mirrored copy turns the other way by itself)
parts.name: front bumper

parts.//: mirrors on the cab's front corners, touching the cab (the game's float 2.5 cm off it: moved in)
parts.name: mirror

parts.//: the tail: tall lamps on the bed's corner posts, tail lamp over brake lamp, set 3 cm into the bed's back
parts.name: tail lamp

parts.//: the rear number plate, its own part (tag plate-rear): the plate cosmetic hides it
parts.name: rear plate

parts.//: RUST as flat colour: thin strips 6 mm proud of the flank, low on the sills and the bed's back corners (the game's own rust is a soft-edged texture; the kit has no textures)
parts.name: rust sill

parts.//: THE LOAD: a loaf of tarpaulin heaped in the bed (a loft: its top rises from the rails at each end to a crest higher than the cab), its hem hanging just outside the rails. It is the cargo slot's own prop (prop: cargo): a cargo cosmetic hides it and the bed stays.
parts.name: tarpaulin

parts.//: green ropes over the tarpaulin: short lofts of the same section grown 1.5 cm, so they stand clear of the cloth (no shared surface)
parts.name: rope

wheels.//: WHEELS UNDER THE BODY: at the body's corners, their tops (0.84) up inside the body (bottom 0.46), so no gap shows over them and no stalk holds them; 30 cm wide, 5 cm proud of the flank. at [x, z]: they sit on the ground (y = radius).

animate.//: a rough idle: the body (everything but the wheels) shudders on its springs

mounts.//: Where cosmetics go. at = the middle of the free area ON the surface; size = [across, along] (decals: [along, up]); height = free space above it.

cargo.note: the bed floor between the wheel tubs; the tarpaulin load is the slot's own prop and is hidden when a cargo cosmetic is fitted

wing.note: the wing's stands on the tailgate top; size [across, along] is its width (78% of the bed's 2.02 m: the game's own Junker wing is 1.58 m) and the stands' footprint; its blade, 0.3 / 1.4 of its width deep (34 cm), may hang over the tail

decals.name: door
decals.note: the cab door below the window, between the wheels

decals.name: bed side
decals.note: the bed's flank over the rear wheel, under the rail
